sentences.text: Researchers used a mouse model of brain bleeding created by injecting an enzyme into the brain, while also growing human brain vessel cells in a lab dish and exposing them to a substance that mimics the post-bleed environment along with the protein Gal-3.
In these cells, the protein Gal-3 attached to a receptor called TLR4 and stopped its normal breakdown, causing the receptor to build up.
This accumulation triggered a chain of chemical signals that increased the production of an enzyme which breaks down the proteins that seal the blood-brain barrier.
The researchers concluded that this process leads to the breakdown of the barrier that protects the brain from the bloodstream.
